summary: A ground-mounted L-4 cab built 1934 or 1935, used as a fire lookout until 1939-1942, now ruined and no longer habitable; access is by hiking.

facts.design: Standard R1/L-4 ground cabin with a Forest design catwalk (NHLR); ground-mounted L-4 cab (Firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: NHLR says it still stands (2020 registration), more than 80 years after last use. A 2024 climbing guide says it is no longer habitable and shows ruins.

staffing.status: no documented staffing history; not staffed after abandonment

visit.trail_note: Listed as hike-in on Idaho Fire Lookouts. The climbing guide describes a route of roughly 2.2 miles from a ridge-top parking spot to the summit and shows photos of the ruins. The cab is no longer habitable.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Salmon-Challis National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1934 for the L-4 cab; the register and the local history page give 1935. The record keeps 1934 with the 1935 date noted.
The register and the local history page put abandonment at 1939 or 1940; Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say 1942. The record keeps 1942 and both dates appear in the events.
The register (2020) says it still stands; the 2024 climbing guide says it is no longer habitable and pictures ruins. Both can be true: the cab stands as a ruin.

notes_for_editor: Access level left unset: no source states public access rules. Staffing as_of is the access date because the Idaho Fire Lookouts staffing note is undated. The CCC training use has no year, so it is in the note text rather than an event. Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Hike-In Abandoned' tag is the only hike-in statement. The Salmon-Challis Forest Service lookouts page was read but names no Greylock detail, so it is not cited. Elevation: NHLR gives 9,850 ft for the lookout location, others give 9,857 ft for the peak. No notable fire was found in the pages read. Brief's status 'standing' kept, with a status_note on deterioration. Photo credit on NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts is 'courtesy of Luke Channer', but no image URL was captured, so no photos were added.
